paper.title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States

selection: gpu_count == 100000; all 34 original columns; pandas CSV serialization

source_sections.load: S1.1; Eq. S1; 8 GPUs/node, 7.3 kW average, 8.5 kW peak, 1.05 design margin
source_sections.degradation: S1.2.3; 1% first-year PV fade then 0.55%/year; BLAST-Lite-derived battery model in upstream only
source_sections.finance: Eqs. 1-2 and S17-S18; S1.3.1; common horizon and midyear discounting
source_sections.limits: Discussion; TMY extremes, supply-side queues as load-interconnection proxy, rental value as opportunity-cost assumption

boundaries: Published CSV values are author-generated model results, not measurements or an independent rerun.
Snapshot includes MV cases only at 100000 GPUs. Upstream smaller facilities also use LV topologies.
Native scenarios are independent screening models with illustrative costs and profiles; they do not implement the authors cooling selection, turbine optimizer, or BLAST-Lite surrogate.
Do not interpret GPU rental value as guaranteed net profit. Opportunity-cost origin and readiness date affect ratios.
